title: TikTok for Business Accounts: How to Set Up, Compare, and Manage Your Brand (Business Center vs Business Manager)
summary: Learn how to create a TikTok Business Account, convert a personal profile, and use Business Center, Business Manager, and the Business App. Compare business vs personal vs creator accounts and pick the right setup for your brand.
body_markdown:
## Business Center vs Business Manager vs Business App: Untangling the Dashboard Ecosystem


Your TikTok profile and your business dashboards serve different jobs. The profile is where people watch and interact with your videos. Business Center is an administrative hub for organizing business assets and granting team access. Ads Manager is where advertisers build and manage campaigns. The term “Business Manager” can appear in business workflows and documentation, but it is not a separate profile type. The TikTok business app, where available, provides a mobile route to business features. Naming and availability can vary, so use TikTok’s current business and ads documentation to confirm the tools shown in your account.


### Tool Glossary: What Each Tool Actually Does


Think of these tools as different workspaces, not account types. Business Center helps organize access to assets such as ad accounts and pixels, and lets administrators assign permissions. Ads Manager supports campaign setup, audience selection, budget management, and performance reporting. A business app gives eligible users access to selected business tasks on mobile. Your TikTok profile remains the public-facing channel for publishing videos and interacting with viewers.


Tool or account Primary role Use it when


Business profile Publishes organic content and represents the brand Your team needs a public TikTok presence


Business Center Organizes assets, access, and permissions Multiple people or accounts need coordinated access


Ads Manager Creates and measures paid campaigns You plan to buy ads and monitor their delivery


Business app Offers selected business tasks on mobile Authorized staff need mobile access to available tools


### Setting Up TikTok Business Center: Ad Accounts, Pixels, and Team Permissions


Start by creating or opening a Business Center through TikTok’s business platform, then confirm who owns it and who will administer access. Add an ad account if your team plans to run paid campaigns, and connect only the assets needed for that work. If you use a TikTok Pixel to measure website actions, configure it with your site and verify that events match the actions you intend to track. Pixel setup supports measurement; it does not replace clear campaign goals or accurate implementation.


Assign permissions according to each person’s responsibilities. An administrator may need broader control than someone who only reviews reporting or helps manage campaigns. Use individual access rather than shared credentials, and remove access when a team member no longer needs it. This setup makes ownership clearer and reduces the risk of accidental changes.


### When You Need Business Manager or the Business App


Use Business Center when several people need structured access to business assets, or when you need to manage advertising resources in one place. Use Ads Manager for paid campaign work; a Business Center by itself does not create a campaign. Choose the business app when your team needs mobile access to the business functions TikTok makes available there. A small team that only publishes organic videos may not need every dashboard. Add tools as your operating needs grow, not simply because they exist.


### How the Pieces Fit Together: Profile vs Dashboard Decisions


Choose the public profile based on how your brand will publish and communicate. Choose dashboards based on who needs access, which assets they manage, and whether you plan to advertise or measure website activity. A practical decision path is: publishing only, start with the profile; paid campaigns, add Ads Manager; shared assets or multiple team members, organize access in Business Center; mobile task management, check whether the business app supports your workflow. A tiktok for business account is the public-facing foundation, while these workspaces support internal operations. Keep the profile owner, business administrators, and ad account permissions documented so your team can work without relying on one person’s login.
